description:
Why: every emptiness decision threads an InFlight path (a parent-linked chain of Frames, src/compiler2/types/emptiness.rs) through tuple, list, resource, function and map clauses, and asks at each step whether the descriptor is already being decided higher up. A descriptor names only descriptors interned before it, so a decision strictly descends and the question is never answered yes. The path is a concept with no job.

What: first prove it. Replace the 'already in flight' answer with a panic and run the whole gate (workspace tests, doc tests, fixture matrix) plus the five OptionParser probes; if it fires anywhere, stop and report the descriptor and the program: the guard has a job and this ticket is rewritten. If it never fires, delete InFlight, Frame, the open parameter on every clause function and their callers, and the branch that reads it.

Signal: identity on the five probes (interp/run stdout, canonical backend dump, activation key and job counts); no pin movement; instructions equal or lower; allocation calls equal or lower.

Removes: InFlight, Frame, the open parameter, the in-flight branch, tests that pin only the guard. Guidepost: .agent/docs on types must state the invariant the deletion rests on (a descriptor names only earlier descriptors) so a future recursive descriptor design knows emptiness needs a path again.
title: Deciding emptiness carries no in-flight path
